paragraphs: Here's what I love about this little passage, friend. Moses knows he won't be crossing the Jordan, because he said, "I must die in this land" (Deuteronomy 4:22). And what does he do with the time he has left? He sets aside three cities so that a man who killed his neighbor "unintentionally without prior malice" has somewhere to run (Deuteronomy 4:41-42). That's a leader thinking about people he may never meet.

Now, I think this part is heavy, so I'll say it once and plainly. A life has been lost, and a life is still on the line. The passage says the man could flee "to save one's own life," and the cities were set aside for that very purpose (Deuteronomy 4:42). Even in the worst day of somebody's life, a way to run was already made, and that tells me something about how seriously God's people were to take every life.

So what do I take from it, baker? Safe places get prepared before anybody needs them. Moses named all three cities, so nobody running scared had to guess where to go (Deuteronomy 4:43). Bezer, Ramoth and Golan were ready and waiting, and that's the kind of readiness I want in my own ovens. The story isn't over yet, so keep baking.
